ORDER:
The instant petition under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 19731 has been filed by the Petitioners/Accused Nos.1 and 2, seeking to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.612 of 2019 on the file of Ongole Taluq Police Station, Prakasam District registered for the offence punishable under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code,1860.2 2.

The facts mentioned in the complaint, in brief, are as follows:
a.

Respondent No.2 participated in the auction conducted by Corporation Bank on 10.08.2018 and being the highest bidder purchased two plots, which are situated on the Southern side of F.C.I. Godowns, Ongole, for an amount of Rs.16,30,000/- and paid an amount of Rs.4,07,500/- towards 25% of the total amount.
Subsequently, he also paid the remaining 75% of the amount within the date prescribed by the Bank Officials and also obtained Sale Confirmation Letter from the said Bank.
for short 'Cr.P.C' for short 'IPC' b.

Thereafter, when Respondent No.2 got surveyed the said land, he came to know that the said plots were not the plots which were shown by the Bank Officials and the plots shown by the Bank Officials were in Court disputes.

c. When the Complainant informed the same the Petitioners/Accused Nos.1 and 2, who are the Chief Manager and Senior Manager of the said Bank respectively,
said that the amount paid by him will be returned with interest.
However, when the Complainant met them recently, the Petitioners told that it is not possible to return the amount and asked him to register the said land as per the document.

d. As such, the complainant lodged a complaint with Ongole Taluq Police and the same was registered as a case in Crime No.612 of 2019 for the offence under Section Rajendra Kumar Patra vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109261681/

sentences.text: 2 420 IPC against the Petitioners/Accused Nos.1 and 2 3.

Aggrieved by the same, Petitioners filed the present petition seeking quashment of the proceedings, on the following grounds:
a. Respondent No.2 after verifying the title deeds available with the bank and after verification of the property, participated in the e-auction and became successful bidder and after payment of entire sale consideration, the Bank confirmed the auction in his favour.
Now he is disputing the identity of the property and demanding for payment of the sale price.
After confirmation of the sale in favour of the complainant, the Bank appropriated the amounts deposited by him towards bid price to the loan account of the actual borrower.
b. Petitioners being the Bank Officers, are always co-operative and are trying to resolve the dispute raised by the complainant and are taking steps to get the land measured by the approved surveyor.
c. The complainant with a malafide intention to create fear and to harass the Petitioners filed the present complaint.
Respondent No.2 is trying to convert the civil dispute as a criminal case and trying to blackmail the petitioners.
d. The Petitioners have no intention to cheat the complainant.
Arguments Advanced at the Bar 4.
Heard Ms.V.Dyumani, learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the State/Respondent No.1.
Though notice was sent to Respondent No.2, none appeared on his behalf to submit arguments.

5. Learned counsel for the Petitioners/Accused Nos.1 and 2 would submit that the Petitioners had never committed any offence as alleged by Respondent No.2 and that they are in fact trying to resolve the issue, but Respondent No.2 with a malafide intention, to gain unlawfully, filed the present petition to harass them.
Before participating in the auction, Respondent No.2 verified all the relevant documents and the existence of the said land.
It is further stated that the allegations leveled against the Petitioners are not tenable.
Hence, prayed to quash the proceedings against the Petitioners.

In support of her contention, learned counsel relied on a decision of the Hon' ble Apex Court in Priyanka Srivastava and another Vs. State of U.P and others3.
6.

sentences.text: A perusal of Section 482 makes it clear that the Code envisages that inherent powers of the High Court are not limited or affected so as to make orders as may be necessary; (i) to give effect to any order under the Code or, (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or, otherwise (iii) to secure ends of justice.
A court while sitting in Section 482 jurisdiction is not functioning as a court of appeal or a court of revision.
It must exercise its powers to do real and substantial justice, depending on the facts and circumstances of the case.

This Court in Gade Venkateswara Rao v. State of A.P.,4 encapsulated this principle in the following terms;
"8.

sentences.text: Section 482 Cr. P.C. powers must be invoked for compelling reasons of abuse of process of law or glaring injustice or violation of sound principles of criminal jurisprudence.
Specific circumstances warranting invocation of powers under Section 482 have been strongly emphasized in a catena of decisions.

To cite a few, State of 2023 SCC OnLine AP 4021 Haryana v. Bhajanlal5 at paras 102 and 103, Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra6 at para 57."
9.

sentences.text: It is a well settled principle of law that when a prosecution is sought to be intervened by quashment, the test to be applied is to see whether the uncontroverted allegations as made prima facie establish the offence alleged or not.

A bare perusal of the material available on record in the present case, would clearly show that, RSR Milk Dairy and RSR Constructions & Developers availed credit facilities from the Corporation Bank, Ongole Branch by offering different properties and subsequently committed default in repayment of the amounts.
As such, The Bank after classifying the account as NPA issued demand notice dated 18.11.2016 under Section 13(2) of the SARFAESI Act.
After following due process under SARFAESI Act, the Bank issued e-auction sale notice dated 23.07.2018 for various properties including the subject property.
10. Having participated in the said auction and having become the successful bidder, Respondent No.2 after payment of the sale price, obtained Sale Certificate dated 04.10.2018 from the Bank.

In due course, bank officials, at the time of taking any property as a security, Bank Panel Advocate gives legal opinion and the Bank's Panel Approved Valuer verifies the property physically and submits valuation report.
11. Any prudent person who intends to purchase a property in an auction, verifies the documents pertaining to the property and as to the existence of the said property.
It is not the case of Respondent No.2 that he had not verified the title deeds available with the bank and the identity of the land.

Further, as per Section 32 of the SARFAESI Act,
no suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against (the Reserve Bank or the Central Registry or any secured creditor or any of its Officers) for anything done or omitted to be done in good faith under the Act.

Furthermore, protection is available to the Authorized Officers of the Bank in discharging their duties, as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Priyanka Srivastava's case (supra).

sentences.text: In the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the Petitioners had no intention to cheat Respondent No.2 at any point of time.
Petitioners are not the owners of the subject property and they have discharged their duties as per the procedure contemplated under SARFAESI Act.
The allegations made in the complaint do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the Petitioners.
There are no tenable grounds to continue the proceedings against the Petitioners in the present crime and as such, the same are liable to be quashed.

13. Accordingly, the criminal petition is allowed quashing the proceedings against the Petitioners/Accused Nos.1 and 2 in Crime No.612 of 2019 on the file of Ongole Taluq Police Station,
Prakasam District for the offence under Section 420 IPC.
